title: Linear recursive teaching dimension versus VC dimension
formal: Is there a universal constant \(c > 0\) such that, for each finite concept class C, we have that \(RTD(C) \le  c \cdot  VCD(C)\)?
why: A universal linear comparison would connect the information needed for recursive teaching with a basic measure of learnability from samples. It tests a general relation across all finite concept classes.

sentences: A finite concept class can be studied through both its VC dimension and its recursive teaching dimension.
VC dimension measures the ability to realize label patterns, while recursive teaching measures how examples can identify concepts through successive elimination.
The question asks whether one universal constant always bounds recursive teaching dimension by that constant times VC dimension.
The same constant must work for every finite class.
The project seeks a direct quantitative link between the complexity of learning from samples and the information needed for structured teaching.

context_blocks.title: Teaching and learning
context_blocks.text: Recursive teaching identifies concepts through successive elimination using selected labeled examples. The 2015 Simon–Zilles question compares its worst teaching cost with VC dimension, which measures the richness of label patterns and governs sample-based learning.

context_blocks.title: Repeated formulation
context_blocks.text: Open Problem 3 of the 2023 paper explicitly returns to the 2015 question: does one constant \(c>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{RTD}(C)\le c\operatorname{VCD}(C)\) for every finite concept class \(C\)? The same constant must work for all classes. Non-clashing teaching dimension and unlabeled sample compression are related but are not substituted for recursive teaching here.

source_consolidations.note: The 2015 Simon–Zilles paper and Open Problem 3 of Simon 2023 ask for the same universal linear upper bound on recursive teaching dimension by VC dimension for finite concept classes. The 2023 question explicitly cites the 2015 source. Non-clashing teaching and sample compression remain different targets.
